gloss: to pluck, to pick, to trim

definitions.explanation: To remove something by pinching with fingers.
To cut off the tips of plants.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}でいちごを{摘|つ}んだ。
examples.english: I picked strawberries in the garden.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると、{子供|こども}たちは{野原|のはら}で{草|くさ}を{摘|つ}んで{遊|あそ}ぶ。
examples.english: When spring comes, children play by picking wild plants in the fields.

examples.japanese: {茶|ちゃ}を{摘|つ}む{季節|きせつ}になると、{畑|はたけ}は{緑|みどり}でいっぱいになる。
examples.english: When the tea-picking season comes, the fields are full of green.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}{早|はや}く{起|お}きて、{露|つゆ}がついたままの{花|はな}を{一|ひと}つずつ{丁寧|ていねい}に{摘|つ}んだ。
examples.english: I got up early in the morning and carefully picked the flowers one by one while they still had dew on them.

examples.japanese: {枝|えだ}の{先|さき}を{摘|つ}んで{整|ととの}える。
examples.english: To trim the tips of branches to tidy up.

examples.japanese: トマトの{脇芽|わきめ}を{摘|つ}まないと、{実|み}が{小|ちい}さくなる。
examples.english: If you don't pinch off the side shoots of tomatoes, the fruit will be small.

examples.japanese: {花|はな}が{咲|さ}く{前|まえ}に{余分|よぶん}なつぼみを{摘|つ}んでおくと、{残|のこ}った{花|はな}が{大|おお}きく{咲|さ}く。
examples.english: If you pinch off the extra buds before they bloom, the remaining flowers will bloom larger.

examples.japanese: {問題|もんだい}の{芽|め}は{早|はや}めに{摘|つ}んでおいたほうがいい。
examples.english: It's better to nip problems in the bud early.
examples.notes: Figurative use of {芽|め}を{摘|つ}む

notes:
{摘|つ}む is a godan verb meaning to pluck or pick with the fingers.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を particle: 〜を{摘|つ}む

ASPECT (ている):
{摘|つ}んでいる describes the ongoing action of picking.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {花|はな}を{摘|つ}む: to pick flowers
- {茶|ちゃ}を{摘|つ}む: to pick tea leaves
- {芽|め}を{摘|つ}む: to nip buds / nip in the bud (also figurative)
- いちごを{摘|つ}む: to pick strawberries

KANJI DISTINCTION (same reading):
- {摘|つ}む: to pluck, pick
- {積|つ}む: to pile up, stack
- {詰|つ}む: to be stuck, checkmated
